title: Pitfalls of vibe testing
detail: Understand the pitfalls of “vibe testing” by examining real-world failure case studies like Air Canada.
qs: Why is vibe testing a poor release gate for an LLM feature?
You changed a prompt and five demo questions look better. What do you do before shipping?

title: Deterministic vs probabilistic testing
detail: Navigate the differences between deterministic software testing and probabilistic LLM systems.
qs: Why can't you simply assert equality on LLM summaries in a unit test?
A test passes locally but fails 1 in 10 runs in CI with temperature 0. How do you handle it?

title: Model evals vs application evals
detail: Distinguish between evaluating core foundation model capabilities and testing complete application workflows.
qs: What is the difference between a model eval and an application eval?
A new model leads a coding leaderboard. Your team wants to swap it in immediately. What should you do?

title: The end-to-end evaluation workflow
detail: Implement an end-to-end evaluation process covering task definition, criteria, datasets, execution, analysis, and iteration.
qs: Walk through the end-to-end evaluation workflow.
Your metrics are green but users complain. Which workflow step has likely been skipped?

title: Unit, slice and end-to-end evals
detail: Test retrieval, generation and the product separately.

title: Vibe testing as a prototype only
detail: Pair it with a frozen set the moment a second person uses the app.

title: Interview
detail: your first eval: 30 cases, expected shape, one judge or checker, run on every prompt change.

title: Who owns the golden set
detail: Product plus engineering; it is a living artefact, not a data-science side quest.

title: Programmatic, human & LLM-as-a-Judge
detail: Categorize evaluation execution mechanisms into Programmatic, Human, and LLM-as-a-Judge approaches.
qs: Compare programmatic, human and LLM-judge evaluation.
Your LLM judge scores long answers higher regardless of quality. How do you detect and mitigate it?

title: Reference-based vs reference-free
detail: Understand reference-based vs reference-free evaluation.
qs: When would you choose reference-free evaluation?
Why can reference-based scoring undercount a correct answer?

title: When a Golden Dataset is required
detail: Determine when a Golden Dataset answer key is required versus when evaluation can rely entirely on LLM judgment.
qs: When is a golden dataset required and when can you do without?
A teammate built 2,000 golden cases by generating variations of 20 prompts. Is that good?

title: Matching method to behaviour
detail: Choose the appropriate evaluation method based on whether the target behavior is deterministic, semantic, subjective, or operational.
qs: Which method would you use to evaluate a JSON extraction task, and which for tone?
Why is using an LLM judge for every check a mistake?

title: LLM-as-judge calibration
detail: Spot-check the judge against humans before you trust the score.

title: Exact-match vs rubric
detail: Use code for format; use a rubric for quality.

title: Interview
detail: pick a method: Programmatic first, human for new failure types, judge for scale.

title: Offline suites for pre-release testing
detail: Use offline evaluation suites for pre-release testing, version comparison, experimentation, and preventing performance regression.
qs: What does an offline eval suite give you that production monitoring does not?
Your offline score improved 3 points but you are unsure it is real. What do you check?

title: Post-deployment production risks
detail: Identify post-deployment production risks including unexpected inputs, emergent systematic failures, changing user behavior, and data drift.
qs: Name production risks that offline evals miss.
Quality dropped last Tuesday but you deployed nothing. What are likely causes?

title: System metrics vs quality metrics
detail: Differentiate automatically captured system metrics such as latency, token usage, and errors from LLM-computed quality metrics such as hallucination or relevance.
qs: Why aren't system metrics enough for LLM apps?
Switching to a cheaper model cut cost 40% with no alerts. What do you verify?

title: Continuous online evaluation pipeline
detail: Implement a continuous online evaluation pipeline through production logging, sampling, dashboarding, and alerting.
qs: Describe the stages of a continuous online eval pipeline.
Why should online scoring be asynchronous and sampled?

title: Feeding failures back offline
detail: Feed important production failures back into the offline evaluation dataset.
qs: How do production failures improve your offline suite?
What risk comes from adding only failures to the dataset?

title: Online shadow traffic
detail: Score production inputs without changing the user reply.

title: Feedback that becomes a case
detail: A thumbs-down with the retrieved context is tomorrow's offline item.

title: Interview
detail: offline vs online: Offline gates a release; online tells you the mix shifted.

title: Core LLM capabilities
detail: Explore core LLM capabilities such as knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, coding, instruction following, long-context understanding, multimodal capability, safety, and tool use.
qs: List core LLM capabilities evaluated by benchmarks.
You build a contract-clause extractor. Which capabilities should drive model choice?

title: Anatomy of a benchmark
detail: Analyze the anatomy of a benchmark through its dataset, prompts, run configuration, scoring method, and result aggregation.
qs: What components make up a benchmark?
Two vendors report different MMLU-style scores for the same model. Why?

title: Public leaderboards
detail: Understand how public leaderboards compare foundation models.
qs: How should an engineer use public leaderboards?
Model A ranks one place above B on a preference leaderboard. Should you pick A?

title: Benchmark pitfalls
detail: Identify benchmark pitfalls including data contamination, score saturation, benchmark overfitting, and configuration gaming.
qs: What is benchmark contamination and why does it matter?
A benchmark shows 97% for several top models. How do you interpret that?

title: Task transfer is the real test
detail: A leaderboard win that fails your tickets is not a win.

title: Reading a model card like a sceptic
detail: Training data, cutoff, safety, and the eval they chose to show.

title: Interview
detail: why you ignored a rank: Contamination, wrong task, or a cost you cannot pay.

title: From MMLU to harder knowledge tests
detail: Trace the progression from benchmarks such as MMLU and TruthfulQA toward harder tests of knowledge and factual reliability.
qs: Why did MMLU lose usefulness for ranking frontier models?
What does the MMLU history teach about relying on a single benchmark?

title: Human exams as benchmarks
detail: Understand the use of human exams in benchmarks such as AGIEval to compare human and model capabilities.
qs: Why are human exams used as LLM benchmarks and what is the catch?
A model passes a medical licensing exam. Can you deploy it for patient advice?

title: GPQA, MMLU-Pro, SimpleQA, HLE
detail: Explore harder benchmarks such as GPQA, MMLU-Pro, SimpleQA, and Humanity's Last Exam.
qs: What gap does SimpleQA address that GPQA does not?
Which benchmark would you check for hallucination tendency on factual lookups and why?

title: Why benchmarks keep getting harder
detail: Understand why benchmarks continually become harder as frontier models saturate older datasets.
qs: Why do benchmarks keep needing to get harder?
What does this trend imply for how long to trust a public benchmark number?

title: Saturation means you need a harder set
detail: When everyone scores 90, the benchmark stopped discriminating.

title: Human exams vs product tasks
detail: GPQA is a filter, not a substitute for your tickets.

title: Evaluating on your actual task
detail: Move beyond public benchmarks and evaluate models on the actual task your application needs to solve.
qs: Why evaluate on your actual task instead of relying on benchmarks?
How many cases do you need to start, and what matters more than count?

title: Shortlisting candidate models
detail: Use leaderboards and aggregation platforms to shortlist candidate models based on capability, latency, context, and cost.
qs: What criteria do you use to shortlist models?
Why include a small cheap model in your shortlist even if you expect it to lose?

title: Building a custom eval dataset
detail: Build a custom evaluation dataset for a real task such as Text-to-SQL.
qs: How do you build a trustworthy custom eval dataset?
Your labels were generated by the same model you are evaluating. What is the problem?

title: Like-for-like model comparison
detail: Compare shortlisted models using the same inputs, prompts, parameters, and scoring criteria.
qs: What must be held constant in a model comparison?
Model B loses to A but your prompt was written while testing A. What do you do?

title: Estimating usage & token cost
detail: Estimate API usage and token costs and use techniques such as prompt caching where appropriate.
qs: How would you estimate monthly LLM cost for a feature?
Your estimate used average prompt size but the bill is double. Why?

title: Quality / latency / cost trade-off
detail: Select the model that offers the best task-specific quality / latency / cost trade-off, rather than simply choosing the highest-ranked general model.
qs: How do you choose between a strong slow model and a cheap fast one?
Name techniques that improve cost or latency without changing the model.

title: Stratify the custom set
detail: Easy, hard, adversarial, and the last five production misses.

title: Cost model beside the quality table
detail: Tokens and latency are columns, not footnotes.

title: Component, pipeline & application levels
detail: Structure evaluations across component level, pipeline level, and application level depending on what is being tested.
qs: Why test components, pipelines and the whole application?
End-to-end score fell but you do not know why. What is your approach?

title: Versioning tests, configs & results
detail: Maintain versioned test cases, evaluation configurations, prompts, models, and results.
qs: What must be versioned to make eval results reproducible?
Scores jumped 6 points overnight with no prompt change. How could versioning help?

title: Experiment tracking & baselines
detail: Track experiments and compare new versions against established baselines.
qs: Why look at flipped cases rather than the average only?
You tuned prompt, model and retrieval simultaneously and the score rose. What is the issue?

title: CI/CD quality gates
detail: Build automated CI/CD quality gates so changes cannot ship when important metrics regress.
qs: How do you design CI quality gates for an LLM app?
The CI eval gate fails randomly and developers start bypassing it. Fix?

title: Self-improving golden dataset
detail: Create a self-improving loop by adding edge cases and failures discovered in production back into the offline golden dataset.
qs: How does a golden dataset improve itself over time?
Why re-score the baseline after adding cases?

title: Quality alongside latency & cost
detail: Track quality together with latency and cost so improvements in one area do not silently damage another.
qs: Why include latency and cost in eval runs?
A prompt change gives +1 quality point and 40% more tokens. How decide?

title: A quality gate in CI
detail: Fail the build on a statistically meaningful drop, not on one flaky case.

title: Baseline you can roll back to
detail: Keep the last shipped prompt and score next to the candidate.

title: Four levels of RAG evaluation
detail: Evaluate a RAG system at component, pipeline, application, and safety levels, rather than treating it as one black-box system.
qs: Name the four levels of RAG evaluation and what each checks.
Why is final-answer-only evaluation inadequate for RAG?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Evaluating the retriever alone
detail: Evaluate the retriever independently to determine whether it finds the information required to answer the question.
qs: How do you evaluate a retriever independently of the LLM?
Why does retriever recall limit the whole RAG system?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Diagnosing missed & noisy retrieval
detail: Diagnose cases where the retriever completely misses the relevant context or retrieves excessive irrelevant/noisy chunks.
qs: How do you distinguish missed from noisy retrieval?
Relevant chunk is at rank 12 and k=5. Fix options?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Retrieval metrics
detail: Measure retrieval effectiveness using metrics such as Contextual Recall, Contextual Precision, Recall@k, and other ranking-aware metrics where appropriate.
qs: Compute recall@5, precision@5 and MRR: relevant {A,B}, retrieved [X,A,Y,Z,W].
Which metric matters most for RAG coverage and why?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Building the Golden Dataset
detail: Generate or curate relevant chunks and ideal answers for a Golden Dataset through hand-authoring, LLM-assisted generation, or tools such as DeepEval's synthetic-data generators.
qs: What does a RAG golden dataset contain?
Why can purely synthetic questions overstate retrieval quality?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Evaluating the generator alone
detail: Evaluate the generator independently by providing known-good context and checking whether it produces faithful and relevant answers.
qs: How do you evaluate a RAG generator in isolation?
The generator invents details even with perfect context. Where do you intervene?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Detecting unfaithful answers
detail: Detect unfaithful claims, irrelevant answers, missing information, and misuse of provided context.
qs: How do you detect an unfaithful RAG answer?
An answer is factually true but not in the context. Is it faithful?

title: [Component-level evaluation] Component tests with DeepEval & RAGAS
detail: Implement component tests using frameworks such as DeepEval or RAGAS while understanding what each metric actually measures.
qs: What do DeepEval and RAGAS provide?
Your RAGAS scores shifted after a library upgrade. What do you do?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] The full retrieve → generate pipeline
detail: Evaluate the complete retrieval → context → generation pipeline.
qs: Why is pipeline-level RAG evaluation needed after component tests?
What should you log for each pipeline run to debug later?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] The RAG Triad
detail: Measure the RAG Triad:
qs: What are the three parts of the RAG Triad and what do low values imply?
Triad scores are all high but users say answers are wrong. Why?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] Contextual Relevancy
detail: Contextual Relevancy
qs: What does contextual relevancy measure, and what does low mean?
Contextual relevancy is 0.95 but answers are incomplete. Which metric is missing?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] Faithfulness
detail: Faithfulness
qs: Define faithfulness and how it is computed.
Can an answer score 1.0 faithfulness and still be bad?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] Answer Relevance
detail: Answer Relevance
qs: What does answer relevance catch that faithfulness doesn't?
A bot copies large passages in reply to a narrow question. Which metrics flag it?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] When good components interact badly
detail: Understand how individually strong components can still interact poorly when connected.
qs: Give examples of interaction failures in a RAG pipeline.
Retriever recall is 95% and generator faithfulness is 95% in isolation but end-to-end accuracy is poor. Where look?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] Diagnosing pipeline-level failures
detail: Diagnose cases such as high retrieval precision but low overall contextual relevance or poor downstream answers.
qs: Outline a step-by-step diagnosis for a wrong RAG answer.
Many failures are 'info not in index'. What does that tell you?

title: [Pipeline-level evaluation] Locating the root failure
detail: Determine whether the root failure lies in retrieval, assembled context, or generation.
qs: How does a gold-context swap help locate the root failure?
Answers hallucinate numbers from tables. Team adds 'do not guess' to the prompt. Comment?

title: [Application-level evaluation] Evaluating from the user's perspective
detail: Evaluate the RAG system from the actual user's perspective rather than only testing internal components.
qs: Why add user-perspective evaluation to component metrics?
Which real-world signals can approximate user satisfaction?

title: [Application-level evaluation] Factual correctness
detail: Measure whether the final answer is factually correct given the available evidence.
qs: Difference between faithfulness and factual correctness?
How would you score correctness for 'The deadline is 15 March 2025, fee 50 dollars' against a reference?

title: [Application-level evaluation] Answer completeness
detail: Evaluate completeness: does the answer address all important parts of the user's request?
qs: How do you measure answer completeness?
Answers are accurate but often miss one of several steps. Likely causes?

title: [Application-level evaluation] Tone, format & citation behaviour
detail: Evaluate application-specific requirements such as tone, style, persona, format, citation behavior, and instruction following.
qs: How would you automatically verify citations in a RAG answer?
Why test format programmatically but tone with a judge?

title: [Application-level evaluation] Operational metrics per query
detail: Track operational metrics including latency, token usage, cost per query, and error rates alongside quality.
qs: Which operational metrics do you record per RAG query?
p95 latency doubled after adding a reranker. How do you investigate?

title: [Safety evaluation for RAG] Harmful & disallowed responses
detail: Evaluate whether the system produces harmful, illegal, dangerous, biased, or otherwise disallowed responses.
qs: Why measure over-refusal alongside harmful compliance?
Your safety judge flags many medical questions as harmful. What do you do?

title: [Safety evaluation for RAG] PII protection & redaction
detail: Test whether sensitive PII such as contact details, credentials, or payment information is appropriately protected or redacted.
qs: How would you evaluate PII protection in a RAG assistant?
Redaction recall is 92% in tests. Is that enough?

title: [Safety evaluation for RAG] Direct & indirect prompt injection
detail: Test direct and indirect prompt injection, including malicious instructions hidden inside retrieved documents.
qs: Explain direct versus indirect prompt injection.
How do you evaluate resistance to indirect injection in a RAG app?

title: [Safety evaluation for RAG] Jailbreak attempts
detail: Test jailbreak attempts intended to bypass application guardrails.
qs: How do you test resistance to jailbreaks over time?
Single-prompt red-team results look clean. What may you be missing?

title: [Safety evaluation for RAG] Poisoned retrieval content
detail: Evaluate whether retrieved malicious or misleading content can manipulate the model into leaking data or ignoring application instructions.
qs: How do you evaluate the impact of poisoned documents on a RAG system?
What index-side controls reduce poisoning risk?

title: Retrieval metrics you actually compute
detail: Recall@k and MRR on a labelled query set.

title: Faithfulness vs answer relevance
detail: A cited lie and an uncited truth fail different tests.

title: Six dimensions of agent evaluation
detail: Evaluate agentic systems at the level of decision-making, trajectories, tool usage, task completion, recovery, and safety.
qs: List six dimensions for evaluating agents.
Why report agent dimensions separately instead of one score?

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Why the final answer is not enough
detail: Understand why evaluating only the final answer is insufficient when an agent autonomously decides how to complete a task.
qs: Give reasons the final answer alone is insufficient for agents.
An agent reports 'refund processed'. How do you verify in an eval?

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Tool selection
detail: Evaluate whether the agent chooses the correct tool for a given situation.
qs: How do you measure tool selection accuracy?
The agent often picks search_orders instead of search_customers. First step?

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Tool argument correctness
detail: Test whether the agent generates accurate and properly formatted tool arguments.
qs: What is the difference between schema validity and argument correctness?
The agent passes order_id values that do not exist. Diagnose.

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Trajectory quality
detail: Evaluate the sequence of actions taken by the agent and whether the trajectory is appropriate for the task.
qs: How can you score trajectory quality when multiple valid paths exist?
A refund must be preceded by identity verification. How do you test it?

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Loops, redundancy & early exit
detail: Detect unnecessary tool calls, redundant actions, loops, incorrect ordering, and premature termination.
qs: How do you detect an agent loop from traces?
The agent says 'done' after one of three required updates. Which failure and how test?

title: [Agent behavior & trajectory evaluation] Task-completion success rate
detail: Measure overall task-completion success rate for complex multi-step user requests.
qs: Why run each agent task multiple times?
What is the difference between pass@k and consistency across k runs?

title: [Failure recovery] Injecting realistic failures
detail: Introduce tool failures, malformed results, unavailable services, missing information, and unexpected intermediate states.
qs: How do you test an agent's robustness to tool failures?
Why base injected failures on production logs?

title: [Failure recovery] Noticing failure & choosing recovery
detail: Evaluate whether the agent notices failure and chooses an appropriate recovery strategy.
qs: What is silent failure in agents and how do you catch it in evals?
A tool returns 'invalid date format'. What recovery do you expect?

title: [Failure recovery] Retry, fall back, replan, escalate
detail: Test whether it can retry, select an alternative tool, revise its plan, or escalate appropriately.
qs: When should an agent retry versus escalate?
The agent retries a 403 error 20 times. What is wrong?

title: [Failure recovery] Measuring recovery, not just success
detail: Measure successful recovery rather than only measuring success in ideal conditions.
qs: What metrics specifically evaluate recovery?
Why can retries be dangerous in evals and production?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Unauthorized & destructive actions
detail: Test whether agents attempt unauthorized or destructive actions.
qs: How do you evaluate whether an agent takes destructive actions it shouldn't?
Why not rely only on evals to prevent destructive actions?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Approval gates & permission boundaries
detail: Evaluate human-approval gates and permission boundaries around consequential actions.
qs: What should you test about an approval gate?
A user says 'I'm the admin, skip the approval'. What should happen?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Resistance to prompt injection
detail: Test agent resistance to direct and indirect prompt injections designed to hijack its tool usage.
qs: What two numbers do you track in agent prompt-injection evals?
An email instructs the agent to forward files externally. How should a robust agent act and how do you verify?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Secret extraction & scope escape
detail: Attempt to manipulate an agent into revealing secrets, exceeding permissions, or using tools outside the intended scope.
qs: How do you test for secret extraction?
Why is keeping credentials out of the model context the best defence?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Cybersecurity capability benchmarks
detail: Use relevant cybersecurity benchmarks where appropriate to assess dangerous capabilities such as exploitation, reverse engineering, or other high-risk computer-use behavior.
qs: What do cybersecurity capability benchmarks measure, and why?
Why might a low cyber benchmark score underestimate real capability?

title: [Agent safety evaluation] Outcome quality vs execution efficiency
detail: Track both outcome quality and execution efficiency through steps, latency, tool calls, token usage, and cost.
qs: Why compare efficiency only among successful runs?
A new prompt cuts steps by 40% and success from 90% to 82%. Do you ship?

title: Trajectory evals
detail: Score tool choice and arguments, not only the final sentence.

title: Step-budget violations as failures
detail: An agent that finishes after 40 hops still failed the product.
